prompt: Construct and run identical 60-second node waypoint missions (seed 7, timestep 0.1 seconds, one waypoint 30 m north and 0 m east) for vehicle-a-otter on planar3 and vehicle-c-azimuth on coupled6. Read both results and report which used less propulsion energy.

output.validation_claim: Planar maneuvering validated at pinned tolerances.

output.name: USV propeller/rudder monohull

output.name: Dual-azimuth overactuated USV
output.validation_claim: Control allocation and composability demonstrated; behavioral dynamics not independently validated.

final_answer_text:
Both runs completed successfully and metrics are confirmed persisted. Results:

| Vehicle | Plant | Completion time (s) | Steps | Propulsion energy | Total energy (incl. sensors) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| vehicle-a-otter | planar3 | 10.10 | 101 | **5.343** | 59.378 |
| vehicle-c-azimuth | coupled6 | 36.80 | 368 | **8.578** | 205.458 |

**Result: vehicle-a-otter (planar3) used less propulsion energy** — 5.34 J-equivalent vs. 8.58 for vehicle-c-azimuth (coupled6), a ~38% reduction.

Notes/caveats:
- Both missions used identical config (seed 7, timestep 0.1 s, single waypoint at 30 m north / 0 m east, node backend), but they did **not** run for the same wall/sim duration to reach that waypoint: the otter reached mission completion in 10.1 s (101 steps) while the azimuth vehicle took 36.8 s (368 steps) — despite `duration_s: 60` being requested for both, the run apparently terminated early at waypoint completion in each case, so the propulsion-energy comparison partly reflects that the azimuth vehicle took much longer (and thus accumulated more energy) to reach the same 30 m waypoint.
- Per the preset registry, `vehicle-c-azimuth` carries a validation caveat: "Control allocation and composability demonstrated; behavioral dynamics not independently validated." Treat its energy/dynamics numbers with corresponding caution — this isn't a validated apples-to-apples dynamic comparison, just a report of what each configured scenario produced.
